subject: Post-call: Redwood integration & SDK questions
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-27T17:05:00-08:00
Subject: Post-call: Redwood integration & SDK questions

Hi Jordan —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Key pain points you shared:
- High latency on your current chat assistant during peak traffic (90th percentile > 1.2s per token).
- Cost pressure: ~4x token spend compared to internal forecasts.
- Need for structured outputs (JSON) from LLM responses to feed downstream workflows and avoid fragile parsing.

Goals you described:
- Replace current endpoint with a solution that gives predictable 99th/90th latency and ~30–50% reduction in per-token cost.
- Ability to call business logic (function calls) from model responses and stream partial results into your UI.
- Evaluate embeddings + reranking for retrieval to reduce prompt size and improve answer relevance.

Integration & product fit notes:
- SDK changes: our client SDK supports streaming responses and a function-calling interface. We typically add a small adapter layer to map your existing handler signatures to Redwood's function call schema.
- Streaming: Redwood streams tokens and structured events; we can stream JSON fragments and include end-of-response structured payloads to make integration easier.
- Structured outputs: we recommend using our structured output validation layer to enforce fields and types before committing data downstream.
- Embeddings/reranking: we suggest a hybrid flow — embeddings for candidate retrieval + model-based reranker for top-K to control latency/cost tradeoffs.

Proposed next steps:
1) I’ll share a short POC plan and a one-page proposal (attached) outlining timeline, success metrics, and roles.
2) Can you send a representative sample of your user prompts + expected structured output examples? (we only need 50–200 examples to start).
3) Schedule POC kickoff next week — I’m available Tue/Wed morning PT.

Attachments: redwood-proposal-v1.pdf (proposal), redwood-poc-plan.md (POC outline)

If that looks right I’ll book a 30-min kickoff and loop in infra for capacity planning.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole | Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0182

Subject: Re: Post-call: Redwood integration & SDK questions

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. This aligns with what we need. A couple clarifying Qs before we lock the kickoff: 

1) Latency SLA — what level of end-to-end 90th/99th latency can Redwood guarantee for the POC? We need to ensure our UI remains snappy.
2) Model variants — do you recommend a specific model family for the reranker vs. the generator? We want to keep costs predictable.
3) Security/compliance — I’ve attached the initial security questionnaire we use for vendor onboarding (ACME-security-reqs.xlsx). Can your team start a SOC2 + data retention discussion?

Also happy to do Tue 9:30am PT for the kickoff if that works for your team.

—Jordan
Jordan Lee | Senior Product Manager, AI
Acme Inc.
jordan.lee@acme.com

Hey Jordan — great questions. Short answers below and I’ve noted long-form details in the POC doc (Drive link below).

1) Latency SLA: For POCs we typically target a 90th percentile token latency under 300ms on our dedicated infra for generation flows; 99th latency depends more on sequence length but we’ll instrument and set a target in the kickoff. We’ll surface 90/95/99 metrics in the POC dashboard so you can verify.

2) Model variants: For retrieval + rerank we recommend a small encoder (cheaper embeddings model) + a lightweight reranker (medium-sized generator) to keep costs down. For final generation we suggest testing two generator variants (one quantized for cost, one higher-fidelity) and compare quality on your evaluation set.

3) Security/compliance: Monica will start the SOC2/data flow thread and we can share our infra architecture and KMS integration notes. Monica — I’ve added the ACME security sheet to the shared Drive.

POC kickoff: Tue 2027-03-02 09:30 PT works for us. I’ll send a calendar invite and include an agenda: goals, success metrics, data samples, infra checklist.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-acme-poc
HubSpot: https://hubspot.com/contacts/HS-1234567

Attachments: redwood-poc-plan.md (POC outline)

Thanks — looking forward.
Marissa
